newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tells factories to clean up their act.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tells factories to clean up their act.

text.p: Bangladeshi industrial plants have been ordered to immediately install waste-treatment facilities on their premises to help curb soil and water pollution, the Daily Star nespaper reported on Tuesday.

The daily, quoting government officials, said the Department of Environment (DOE) had identified some 1,167 industrial plants as the nation's "worst polluters" and served notice on them to set up waste-treatment facilities.
Industrial plants in and around the capital Dhaka discharge about 14,000 tonnes of solid waste and 16,000 tonnes of chemical waste into rivers every year, according to a recent DOE survey.

Hundreds of other plants across the country release 35,000 cubic metres of untreated waste into rivers and other bodies of water, causing gross pollution of river water and low plains, the survey said.

Fertiliser units, pulp and paper mills, tanneries, textile dyeing and printing mills, iron and steel mills and cement factories were among the "worst polluters", environment officials were quoted as saying.
Most Bangladeshi industries do not have waste-treatment facilities.
